findings.title: Portable boundary validation trusts stored status instead of checking the recorded changed-path set
findings.observed: In the actual c75dc268 depth-1 detached checkout, the ordinary no-env Vitest command exits 0 after scope-audit.boundaryProof.changed receives an unowned apps/docs/src/pages/unowned-review-probe.astro path. It also exits 0 when the required search-contract.spec.ts repair is removed from that list. All current source/receipt hashes remain unchanged. Both JSON mutations were restored byte-exactly.
findings.cause: readAndValidateScopeAudit validates implementationPaths, receiptPaths, hash keys, and stored withinBoundary/empty error arrays, but never derives the permitted inventory from boundaryProof.changed and proofRecords. The newly added portableInventory emits productSourceChanged=[] and productSourceByteUnchanged=true regardless of that path list.
findings.fix: Recompute the boundary from the recorded changed-path set: reject duplicates, unknown paths, missing required repair/evidence paths, and inconsistent proofRecords. Permit only explicitly owned proof metadata paths. Compare the recomputed implementation set with IMPLEMENTATION_PATHS and ensure stored summaries agree. Derive productSourceChanged and byte-unchanged status from the validated inventory instead of hardcoding success. Add real ordinary-mode negative probes for an added unowned product path and an omitted required repair, preserving source/receipt byte tamper tests. Keep actual task-time Git auditing, seven real selector proofs, and external aggregate completion requirement intact.
findings.not_an_allegation: The unmodified committed audit matches the real Git boundary and all 17 byte hashes. This finding concerns the verifier accepting a contradictory record, not fabricated author evidence.
